questions.prompt: Which PROUD value does Module B anchor on?
options: Show Respect
Encourage Unity
Seek Opportunity
Bring Positivity
questions.explanation: The PROUD value anchor is Seek Opportunity.

options: Final outcomes and progression
Freshers activities
Building foundations
Settling in

questions.prompt: What happens to gaps from Year 1 in Year 2?
options: They're forgiven by staff
They disappear over the summer
They get covered in a refresher week
They compound - what you didn't consolidate in Year 1 is what you hand in for final assessment
questions.explanation: Gaps from Year 1 don't disappear - they compound.

questions.prompt: When does a missed brief actually hurt you, according to the deck?
options: The week you miss it
Never, if you explain it
Only at the end of Year 2
At the portfolio deadline, when you're catching up and trying to produce new work simultaneously
questions.explanation: It hurts you at the portfolio deadline, when you're catching up and trying to produce new work simultaneously.

questions.prompt: Which are the three 'Seek Opportunity' Year 2 moves? Select all that apply.
options: Make progression concrete this year - it's active now, not pending
Build something to talk about - applications need things to have actually happened
Wait for someone to offer you a placement
Treat Year 2 setbacks as information - course-correct now, not in June
questions.explanation: Make progression concrete, build something to talk about, treat setbacks as information.

questions.prompt: What is 'the wall trap' in Year 2?
options: The college's server goes down during deadline week
Hitting a literal wall in a shoot
Year 2 pressure is real and you don't want to admit you're struggling, so you don't ask
You forget your login for Pro Portal
questions.explanation: The wall trap: pressure is real and you don't want to admit you're struggling, so you don't ask.

questions.prompt: How do staff writing references remember attendance, according to the deck?
options: They remember who showed up in Year 2, not just Year 1
They use a database; it's all automatic
They only ask for Year 1 attendance
They use the same letter for everyone
questions.explanation: References are written from memory - staff remember who showed up in Year 2, not just Year 1.

questions.prompt: Why does the deck ask for one habit, not five?
options: Five is too many words for a card
The teacher can only mark one answer
Habits change behaviour; five at once is a plan - which means none of them happen
Five cards cost more to print
questions.explanation: Habits change behaviour. Plans don't. Five at once is a plan - which means none of them happen.
